words_to_read_new.meaning: act means to do + -ive means relating to: relating to doing things
co- means together + oper means work + -ative means relating to: relating to working together
af- means to + firm means strong + -ative means relating to: relating to saying yes firmly
neg means no or deny + -ative means relating to: relating to saying no
in- means into + quis means seek + -ive means relating to: relating to seeking into everything
sens means feel + -ive means relating to: relating to feeling things quickly
ex- means out + plos means burst + -ive means relating to: relating to bursting out
prim means first + -ive means relating to: relating to the earliest times
as- means to + sert means put + -ive means relating to: relating to putting your view firmly
re- means back + strict means draw tight + -ive means relating to: relating to holding back tightly
ex- means out + haust means drain + -ive means relating to: relating to drawing out every last bit
suc- means after + cess means go + -ive means relating to: relating to going one after another

sessions.wtr_new_notes:
READ each word as it appears, then connect -ive to the card meaning: relating to, like.
active - act means to do + -ive means relating to: relating to doing things. Always busy!
cooperative - co- means together + oper means work + -ative means relating to: relating to working together. A helpful team player!
affirmative - af- means to + firm means strong + -ative means relating to: relating to saying yes firmly. The opposite of a no!
negative - neg means no or deny + -ative means relating to: relating to saying no. A minus, not a plus!
inquisitive - in- means into + quis means seek + -ive means relating to: relating to seeking into everything. Very curious!
sensitive - sens means feel + -ive means relating to: relating to feeling things quickly.
explosive - ex- means out + plos means burst + -ive means relating to: relating to bursting out.
primitive - prim means first + -ive means relating to: relating to the earliest times.
assertive - as- means to + sert means put + -ive means relating to: relating to putting your view firmly.
restrictive - re- means back + strict means draw tight + -ive means relating to: relating to holding something back tightly.
exhaustive - ex- means out + haust means drain + -ive means relating to: relating to drawing out every last bit. Nothing left out!
successive - suc- means after + cess means go + -ive means relating to: relating to going one after another.
POINT OUT: after a base ending in -ate, the ending you see and hear is -ative. Cooperate becomes cooperative; negate becomes negative.
Memory hook: -IVE means it is like that, it does that. Chant the pairs: act - active, sense - sensitive, cooperate - cooperative.

grammar.header_notes:
PURPOSE: Introduce adverbials - the part that tells when, where, how or why.
PREP: Have whiteboards ready before the I do.

i_do.title: What is an adverbial?
i_do.rule: An adverbial tells when, where, how or why something happens.
i_do.example: We built the shelter after the storm.
items: After the storm tells us WHEN we built it.
An adverbial can be one word or a group of words.
i_do.routine: Eyes on me - watch the test
i_do.footer: Tomorrow: move the adverbial to the front
i_do.notes:
ANSWER: after the storm - it tells when we built the shelter.
1. SAY: "An adverbial is the part of a sentence that tells when, where, how or why. Some of you may remember prepositional phrases from last week; most adverbials are built the same way."
2. MODEL: Point to after the storm. SAY: "I ask myself, when did we build it? The answer is after the storm, so that group of words is the adverbial."
3. ASK: "What does after the storm tell us?" 5 sec, choral response. EXPECT: when.
4. CHECK: Ask, "Does the shelter tell when, where, how or why?" EXPECT: no.
TRAP: choosing the shelter because it is a thing in the sentence. Fix: run the when, where, how or why test, then point to after the storm.
---
Purpose: first exposure this week; bridge from last week's prepositional phrases. [I Do | Explicit modelling | Grammar | HITS 3]

we_do.title: Find the adverbial
we_do.rule: An adverbial tells when, where, how or why something happens.
we_do.example: The possum crept along the fence.
items: Write the adverbial on your board, boards up together.
Prove it: does it tell when, where, how or why?
we_do.footer: Stem: It is an adverbial because it tells ...
we_do.notes:
ANSWER: along the fence - it tells where the possum crept.
1. SAY: "Write the group of words that tells when, where, how or why. Write it... chin it... show me."
2. TIME: 15 seconds, then boards up together.
3. SCAN the back row first. 80%+ -> ask for the reason. Less -> model with "She sang beautifully", then re-ask.
4. ASK: "How do you know along the fence is the adverbial?" 5 sec, choral response. EXPECT: it tells where the possum crept.
TRAP: writing only the word fence. Fix: ask the where question again, then take the whole group of words.
---
Purpose: guided identification with the when, where, how or why test. [We Do | Guided practice | Grammar | HITS 7]

you_do.title: Your turn
you_do.rule: Write the adverbial from each sentence, then write its job: when, where, how or why.
you_do.example: One done for you: We ate lunch under the gum tree. Adverbial: under the gum tree (where)
items: 2. Mia finished her project without any help.
you_do.routine: Whiteboards - 90 seconds - boards up when done
you_do.footer: The whole group of words, not just one word
you_do.notes:
ANSWER: 1. at dawn (when). 2. without any help (how).
1. SAY: "Write the adverbial from each sentence, then write its job: when, where, how or why."
2. TIME: 90 seconds. Work independently on whiteboards.
3. CIRCULATE: if a student is stuck, SAY: "Look at the worked example - under the gum tree tells where. Now ask your sentence, when did the kookaburra laugh?" Then write number 1 together.
4. SCAN four boards. 80%+ -> reveal the check slide. Less -> run the job test aloud on number 1, then re-check.
TRAP: writing only dawn. Fix: ask the when question again, then take the whole group of words.
STRETCH: Write your own sentence with an adverbial that tells why.
HELP: Give when, where, how, why as a word bank; students match a job to each underlined adverbial.
---
Purpose: independent identification before tomorrow's position switch. [You Do | Independent practice | Grammar | HITS 5]
you_do.check_title: Tick it or fix it - Your turn
you_do.check_rule: Tick each correct adverbial. Fix any that is wrong.
check_items: it tells when the kookaburra laughed
it tells how Mia finished her project
you_do.check_footer: The whole group of words, not just one word
you_do.check_notes:

1. REVEAL after every board has been scanned. MODEL: SAY: "Number 1: I ask when did the kookaburra laugh? At dawn. So the adverbial is at dawn and its job is when."
2. SAY: "Tick each correct answer. Fix any that is different."
3. ASK: "Why is dawn on its own not enough?" 10 sec, turn and tell. EXPECT: at dawn is the whole group of words that answers when.

TRAP: ticking a one-word answer. Fix: reread the whole group of words, then correct it.
STRETCH: Explain why without any help tells how and not why.
HELP: read the green answer first, then match the job word to it.

sessions.wtr_new_notes:
READ each word as it appears, then connect -ite to the card meaning: native of, quality, mineral.
graphite - graph means write or draw + -ite means mineral: the mineral you write with. It is the grey stuff inside a pencil!
pyrite - pyr means fire + -ite means mineral: the mineral that sparks like fire. Fool's gold!
granite - gran means grain + -ite means mineral: the rock with hard grains packed through it.
dynamite - dynam means power + -ite means mineral or substance: the substance packed with power.
composite - com- means together + pos means put + -ite means having the quality of: having the quality of being put together from parts.
definite - de- means completely + fin means end or limit + -ite means having the quality of: having a fixed limit. No doubt at all!
infinite - in- means not + fin means end + -ite means having the quality of: having no end at all.
exquisite - ex- means out + quis means seek + -ite means having the quality of: worth seeking out. Beautiful and rare!
favourite - favour means liking + -ite means having the quality of: the one you like most.
appetite - ap- means towards + pet means seek + -ite means having the quality of: seeking food. Hunger!
suburbanite - sub- means near + urban means city + -ite means native of: a person who lives near the city.
hypocrite - hypo- means under + crit means judge + -ite means one who: one who judges others from behind a mask. They say one thing and do another!
Memory hook: -ITE has three jobs - a MINERAL like graphite, a PERSON like suburbanite, or a QUALITY like definite. Chant it: rock, person, quality.

grammar.header_notes:
PURPOSE: Move an adverbial to the front and back again, and punctuate it.
PREP: Have whiteboards ready before the I do.

i_do.title: Move the adverbial
i_do.rule: An adverbial tells when, where, how or why. It can move to the front of the sentence.
i_do.example: We built the shelter after the storm. -> After the storm, we built the shelter.
items: Move it to the front and add a comma.
The meaning stays the same; the emphasis changes.
i_do.routine: Eyes on me - watch the move
i_do.footer: Next: you move them both ways
i_do.notes:
ANSWER: After the storm, we built the shelter.
1. SAY: "An adverbial tells when, where, how or why. Today we learn that it can move. If this feels new, that's okay - we'll build it together."
2. MODEL: Point to after the storm. SAY: "I lift the adverbial off the end, put it at the front, and drop a comma in behind it."
3. ASK: "What did I add after the fronted adverbial?" 5 sec, choral response. EXPECT: a comma.
4. CHECK: Ask, "Did the meaning change?" EXPECT: no - only what the reader notices first.
TRAP: forgetting the comma after a fronted adverbial. Fix: read it aloud, hear the pause, then add the comma.

Purpose: restate the adverbial rule, then extend it to position. [I Do | Explicit modelling | Grammar | HITS 3]

we_do.title: Front it or end it
we_do.rule: An adverbial can sit at the front or at the end. A fronted adverbial takes a comma.
we_do.example: In the science lab, we tested the graphite.
items: Move the adverbial to the end and write the new sentence.
Decide: does it still need the comma?
we_do.notes:
ANSWER: We tested the graphite in the science lab. No comma is needed.
1. SAY: "Move the adverbial to the end, write the whole new sentence, then decide about the comma. Write it... chin it... show me."
2. TIME: 30 seconds, then boards up together.
3. SCAN the back row first. 80%+ -> ask for the reason. Less -> move it together aloud, then re-ask.
4. ASK: "Why does the comma disappear?" 5 sec, choral response. EXPECT: the adverbial is no longer at the front.
